extracted.intended_audience: Mystery/crime short-story authors and publishers submitting to the Edgar Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility rules and implicit quality expectations for short stories submitted to the Mystery Writers of America's Edgar Award (Short Story category). Covers procedural submission requirements (word count, publication, payment, publisher) and the literary criteria MWA values in mystery short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: First publication timing and place
rubrics_metrics.description: First publication in U.S. during the eligibility year

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre/field membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Mystery, crime, suspense, or intrigue field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must belong to the mystery/crime/suspense/intrigue genres to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher approval
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publisher of the work must be approved by the Mystery Writers of America (MWA) for eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author payment requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Author must have received ≥ $25 in advance/royalties
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must have been paid at least $25 (advance or royalties) for the work to qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong central puzzle / crime / suspense engine
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong central puzzle / crime / suspense engine
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story should be driven by a clear mystery, crime, or suspense mechanism that propels the plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clued solution / fair play or earned reveal
rubrics_metrics.description: Clued solution — fair play (cozy/whodunit) or earned reveal (suspense)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For whodunit/cozy-style stories, the solution should be 'clued' (fair play); for suspense-oriented pieces, revelations should feel earned rather than arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling investigator/protagonist with distinct voice
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protagonists or investigators should be compelling and have a distinct narrative voice that engages the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twist or revelatory recontextualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Twist or revelation that recontextualizes earlier events
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong story may include a twist or revelation which causes readers to reinterpret prior events in the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate atmosphere
rubrics_metrics.description: Atmosphere appropriate to subgenre (noir darkness, cozy charm, thriller momentum)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tone and atmosphere should match subgenre expectations (examples given: noir darkness, cozy charm, thriller momentum).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The story should use economical setup and maintain or escalate tension effectively throughout the piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: Moral resonance — crime fiction often carries ethical weight
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories often benefit from carrying ethical or moral weight, prompting reflection beyond the puzzle or plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subgenres recognized
rubrics_metrics.description: Hardboiled / noir; Cozy mystery; Police procedural; Psychological suspense; Historical mystery; International / crime; Caper / heist
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The category recognizes a range of mystery/crime subgenres, indicating breadth of acceptable styles and settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robert L. Fish Memorial Award (special award) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Robert L. Fish Memorial Award — best first mystery short story by an American
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special award for the best first mystery short story by an American author (separate recognition within MWA awards).
